subject: APAC edge residency assertion and PrivateLink trace pack request

From: Sana Patel <sana.patel@medstar.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: APAC edge residency proof and PrivateLink traces

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this — Signet's compliance team has followed up with a tranche of questions tied to our SOC2/SIG review. They need proof that traffic for Signet's tenant in APAC terminates on infrastructure physically located in the Singapore region, and confirmation that PrivateLink (privatelink-redwood-sg) peering does not route traffic out of APAC. Specifically they asked for:

- A short packet/traceroute sample showing egress/ingress path from a probe inside the Signet test VPC to the model serving endpoint (timestamps and IP prefixes OK).
- A topology diagram of the PrivateLink connection annotated with POPs and the peering ACLs.
- A statement of any maintenance/failover routing that could cause ephemeral cross-region egress.

Can you share a "trace pack" (sanitized traceroutes + diagram + short statement) we can hand to their auditors? They prefer non-sensitive artifacts — ASNs/IP prefixes + last-hop datacenter names are fine, but please remove any customer IPs/keys.

Appreciate a target of EOD Thu (3/4) if possible — Signet is on a tight audit timeline.

Best,
Sana
Sana Patel
Senior Security Programs Manager
Signet Health

Rohan / Sofia,

Attached: apac-edge-traceroutes-20270228.txt, privatelink-topology-diagram-annotated.pdf, keystore-partition-map-anon.csv.

Summary of evidence included:
- Traceroutes: three independent probes (SG1-ops, SG1-probe-b, SG1-control) to the serving VIPs. Each sample lists hop ASN and regional POP nodename. All last-hops terminate in the SG region (Southeast Asia POPs) and indicate no intermediate egress to EU/US ASNs. Sensitive customer IPs have been replaced with 10.0.x.x placeholders.
- Topology diagram: shows PrivateLink endpoint in the Signet VPC -> privatelink-redwood-sg -> SG serving subnet. Annotated with peering ACL references and a note that BGP is not advertised to external transit for these endpoints.
- Keystore map: shows KMS partitions mapped to regional keystores (SG-only partitions for Signet workload). Keys are anonymized; HSM partition IDs are redacted.

Ops note (for auditors):
- Under normal operation, serving traffic for Signet in APAC is pinned to SG-local serving nodes via Smart Routing policy (region: sg).
- Auto-failover promotes standby nodes in the same SG region. If SG fleet is unavailable (full-region outage) we have a documented cross-region fallback policy which requires manual escalation and is triggered only if failover playbook OOS-REGION-01 is executed.
- We do not advertise PrivateLink endpoints to public transit; egress to non-APAC regions requires manual routing changes and takes 2+ hours under our change-control process.

References included: CAIQ section pointers (networking, partitioning), SOC 2 control IDs mapped to key artifacts.

Please review. If this looks good I'll send the trace pack to Sana with a short attestation.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Applied Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sana — attaching the trace pack for Signet's audit.

Included artifacts:
- apac-edge-traceroutes-20270228.txt (sanitized traceroutes; ASNs and POP nodenames retained)
- privatelink-topology-diagram-annotated.pdf (annotated topology and ACL references)
- keystore-partition-map-anon.csv (anonymized keystore partition mapping)

Short attestation: Redwood Inference confirms that, based on current configuration and observed traceroutes, traffic from Signet's APAC PrivateLink endpoints terminates on SG-region serving nodes and does not traverse EU/US networks during normal operation. Cross-region routing for serving traffic is possible only via an explicit, documented escalation and change-control process (referenced runbook OOS-REGION-01).

If compliance needs an executed packet capture instead of traceroute samples we can arrange a controlled capture under an NDA; please advise.
